title: Risk Management
big_picture: A clearing corporation promises every buyer their shares and every seller their money, even if a broker goes bust. To keep that promise it behaves like a cautious landlord: it takes a deposit before you trade (VaR, ELM, SPAN), checks the meter every day (mark to market), pulls the plug when someone gets too big or too stretched (position limits, risk reduction mode, circuit breakers) and keeps a disaster fund with a strict order of who pays first (Core SGF). The rest of the chapter is the broker's side of the bargain: collect margins from clients upfront, protect client money and securities, and file the right report on the right date.
exam_focus: Cash segment margins: VaR group rates (Group I min 9%, Group II min 21.5%, Group III 50%/75%), ELM 3.5% (2% for index ETFs), TFTS 100%, MTM grossed across clients, 20% minimum upfront, T+5 reporting.

Derivatives margins: SPAN (16 scenarios, 99% VaR, MPOR at least 2 days), ELM table and deep-OTM rates, calendar spread charges (1.75% / 2.2%), delivery margin 4 days before expiry, upfront option premium, expiry-day extra 2% ELM.
New in July 2026: no calendar spread benefit on expiry day only for spreads involving the expiring contract (the 29th/30th/31st illustration).

New in July 2026: unpaid securities auto-pledged to the CUSPA, 5 trading days to pay, auto-release at end of 6th day, extension request by 6 p.m. on 5th day for one calendar week, no bank/NBFC pledge, no exposure.

Thresholds that look alike: RRM at 90% and exit below 85%; MWPL ban at 95%; circuit breakers 10/15/20%; cash equivalents at least 50%; single bank 20%; liquid net worth ₹50 lakh; BMC ₹10/15/25/50 lakh.
Client protection: margin pledge chain, peak margin snapshots (minimum 4, higher shortfall penalised), collateral blocking order, upstreaming of client funds, UPI block / 3-in-1 for QSBs.

Deadlines and Core SGF: STR 7 days, CTR/NTR by 15th, Annual Global Statement within 30 days of FY end, half-yearly reports within 2 months; Core SGF 50/25/25 shares, MRC by 15th, default waterfall order.

sections.title: Cash Segment Risk Framework: The Big Picture

blocks.text: A clearing corporation (CC) gives a settlement guarantee: funds and securities get settled even if a broker/clearing member fails. To survive such failures it follows SEBI's risk management measures. The risk management system must be well documented and accessible to clients and the Exchange/CC.

Think of the CC as a landlord guaranteeing everyone's rent: a deposit before you move in (upfront margins), a meter reading every night (MTM), a cut-off for tenants who overspend (limits, risk reduction mode) and a repair fund (Core SGF).

Upfront rule. As in derivatives, TMs/CMs must collect VaR margin and ELM upfront from cash segment clients. Other margins (MTM, delivery, special) are payable on call, but for penalty purposes brokers get until settlement day to collect them. That window is for practical difficulties, not a right for clients to pay late.

items: Full pay-in of funds and securities by settlement day = all other margins deemed collected. Otherwise, penalties.
No need to collect MTM if initial margins already cover the potential loss.
No short-collection penalty if a minimum 20% upfront margin is collected in lieu of VaR and ELM.
Actual/short/non-collection is reported to the Exchange on a T+5 basis.

blocks.text: Riya buys 1,000 shares of a Group I stock at ₹500 = ₹5,00,000. VaR 9% + ELM 3.5% = ₹62,500. Her broker takes ₹1,00,000 (20%) upfront, so no short-collection penalty can arise. If an MTM call follows, the broker has until settlement day; if Riya completes full pay-in by then, it counts as collected.

CC risk containment includes capital adequacy of members, monitoring of member performance and track record, stringent margins, position limits based on capital, online monitoring of positions and automatic disablement from trading when limits are breached. Other salient features (cash and derivatives): online real-time risk management, online monitoring of margin against liquid assets and of position limits, scientific margin levels, different margins for different losses, intraday and EOD MTM, client-level collateral segregation, alerts at various collateral-utilisation levels, risk reduction mode and cross margining.

blocks.text: Mean impact cost = average % price move caused by a hypothetical ₹1 lakh order versus the mean of best bid and offer (ideal price), from 4 random snapshots a day in fixed 10-minute windows, over 6 months, buy and sell sides. Exchanges use a common method and publish results on their websites.
Best bid ₹99.90, best offer ₹100.10: ideal price ₹100. A ₹1 lakh buy order fills at an average ₹100.50, so impact cost = 0.5%. Traded on 80%+ of days too? Then it is Group I.

blocks.text: VaR collection: upfront at the time of trade, on the gross open position = gross of all net positions of all clients plus proprietary, with no netting across settlements. Rates are updated at least 5 times a day: previous close at start, 11:00 a.m., 12:30 p.m., 2:00 p.m. and end of day.

Add the absolute nets per security per settlement: X/2005001 = 100 + 2,100 = 2,200; Y/2005001 = 950; Z/2005001 = 150; X/2005002 = 0; Y/2005002 = 450 + 1,350 = 1,800; Z/2005002 = 3,450 + 1,050 = 4,500. C's net sale in Z does not cancel the prop net buy in Z.
blocks.title: Gross open position

blocks.text: Gross open position = net within each client, gross across clients. Never netted across clients or across settlements.

ELM covers losses beyond VaR: 3.5% for any stock, 2% for broad-based index ETFs. Real time, on gross open position, no netting across settlements, released on completion of pay-in. It replaced the terms 'exposure limits' and 'second line of defence'.
Trade for Trade Surveillance (TFTS) securities: upfront margin (VaR + ELM) = 100%.

MTM loss: each transaction is marked to the day's closing price (latest available close if untraded). If the net position is nil, the buy-sell difference is a notional loss. MTM is computed client by client and only losses are added at broker level.
Client A: X +₹300, Y −₹1,200 = −₹900. Client B: Z −₹1,300, Y +₹200 = −₹1,100. Client C: +₹1,400. Broker pays ₹900 + ₹1,100 = ₹2,000; C's profit cannot cover A and B.
blocks.title: MTM grossed across clients

items: Collected before the start of next day's trading, only from the cash/cash-equivalent part of liquid assets.
TFTS: each trade is marked to market at the closing price.
No set-off across two settlements (T+1 and T+0); netting is allowed within the day's MTM computation. Released with pay-in, including early pay-in.

blocks.text: Intraday Crystallised MTM (ICMTM) catches losses on positions opened and closed the same day, which would never appear in an EOD position. It is computed at weighted average prices on trades subject to upfront margining, adjusted against liquid assets in real time, netted across securities of the same client (not across two rolling settlements), grossed across clients and prop, not computed for TFTS, included in EOD MTM, and released on pay-in/early pay-in. If crystallised losses exceed free collateral, the entity goes into risk reduction mode.
A client buys 200 shares at an average ₹1,000 and sells them by noon at ₹985. Flat position, but ₹3,000 lost: ICMTM blocks it at once.
Highly volatile stocks (also applies in F&O). Intraday move = max of (High − Low), (High − Previous Close), (Low − Previous Close).

Margin caps. Buy: VaR + ELM + MTM together cannot exceed the purchase value (a buyer can't lose more than he paid). Sale: VaR + ELM cannot exceed the sale value, and MTM is levied on top (a seller's loss grows as the price rises).

A member deposits ₹40 lakh cash/FDs and ₹70 lakh of approved shares (post-haircut). Only ₹40 lakh of shares counts: liquid assets = ₹80 lakh, and MTM must come from the ₹40 lakh cash part.

Institutional trades pay normal margins but are exempt from upfront collection: margined on a T+1 basis, collected from the custodian on confirmation. Rejected/unaccepted by the custodian → margin levied on the executing member. Institutions here: Category I and II FPIs (not corporate bodies, individuals or family offices), MFs, public financial institutions (Sec 2(72), Companies Act 2013), banks (Sec 5(1)(c), Banking Regulation Act 1949), IRDA-registered insurers and PFRDA-registered pension funds.
Category II FPIs that are corporate bodies, individuals or family offices are margined upfront, like non-institutional clients.
Pre-open call auction (including IPO and re-listed scrips) uses order-level risk checks: an order without enough available capital for its margin is not accepted.

sections.title: Margin Shortfall and Base Minimum Capital

blocks.text: A margin shortfall violates CC rules and attracts penalty. The CC may advise the Exchange to withdraw the CM's membership rights, including trading facilities of all its TMs and clearing for its custodial participants, and may, without further notice, close out positions, levy penalties, collect deposits or invoke BGs/FDRs.
Base Minimum Capital (BMC) is a deposit for contingencies in any segment. It gives no exposure.
10-15-25-50: prop only, clients only, both, any algo.

items: Several segments of the same exchange: pay the highest BMC, not the sum. Exchanges may ask for more.
At least 50% in cash and cash equivalents.
Exchanges without nation-wide terminals: 40% of these amounts.
BMC is maintained at ₹1 lakh if average daily turnover is below ₹1 crore for any three consecutive months.

sections.title: Additional Margins and Early Pay-in

blocks.text: Exchanges/CCs may add risk measures beyond SEBI's. Ad-hoc margins should only cover situations not anticipated in the system design; if used regularly, the exchange should build them into the system. They must rest on objective criteria and not discriminate between members subjectively.

Early pay-in (EPI). Funds or securities paid in early are excluded from margin computation to that extent. EPI of securities = all margins deemed collected, so no short-collection penalty. SEBI's July 16, 2021 circular brought a block mechanism: the seller's shares stay in his demat, blocked in favour of the CC, which matches the block with the client's net obligation. Mandatory for all EPI from November 14, 2022; not applicable to clients clearing through custodians.
Meera sells 500 shares worth ₹2,000 each. Her broker blocks them in her demat for the CC on trade day: the ₹10 lakh sell position needs no margin.

blocks.text: Pre-order checks act before an order enters the system; pre-trade checks act before execution. Some are run by the TM, some by the exchange. Orders in stocks under surveillance (GSM, ASM, ESM, unsolicited SMS/videos) trigger an alert on the terminal.

Client-level cumulative open order value check (limit set by broker)

blocks.text: Price bands. In 2001 SEBI set scrip-wise bands of 2% to 20% for compulsory rolling settlement scrips, except those with derivatives, which got dynamic bands. The revised dynamic band is 10% of previous close/adjusted base price for F&O stocks, index futures and stock futures. Features: uniform flexing across exchanges; tiered flexing of 5%, 3%, 2% after cooling-off periods of 15, 30, 60 minutes; sliding bands (opposite band moves too); temporary price floors/ceilings for options during the underlying's cooling-off.
An F&O stock closed at ₹1,000, so today's dynamic band is ₹900 to ₹1,100. A buy order at ₹1,150 is rejected at entry: a pre-order check.
blocks.title: Dynamic price band

blocks.text: Market-wide circuit breakers trigger at 10%, 15% and 20% moves of the BSE Sensex or NSE Nifty 50, whichever is breached first.
20% ends the day any time. 15% ends it after 2 p.m. 10% after 2:30 p.m. does nothing.
Circuit breakers are index-based (Sensex or Nifty 50, whichever is breached first). Stock-level limits are price bands, a different tool.

sections.title: Risk Reduction Mode

blocks.text: When 90% of a broker's collateral available for margins is used, the exchange/CC must put it in risk reduction mode (RRM): it can cut risk but not add to it.

items: All unexecuted orders are cancelled. Only Immediate or Cancel orders are allowed.
New orders are checked for margin: risk-reducing orders are accepted; risk-increasing ones without enough margin are rejected. Non-margined orders are not accepted.
No orders with custodial participant code; no client code or CP code modification.
Back to normal mode when utilisation falls below 85% (current CC level).

blocks.text: Enter RRM at 90% collateral utilisation; exit below 85%. Example: ₹10 crore collateral → RRM at ₹9 crore used, normal again below ₹8.5 crore.

With client-level segregation, only the part of a client's margin above 90% of that client's own collateral spills onto the broker. TM level: these client excesses + TM prop margin are tested against TM prop collateral. CM level: each TM's excess above 90% of its prop collateral, + excesses of the CM's own clients + CM prop margin, are tested against CM prop collateral.

TM prop collateral ₹1 crore. Client X: collateral ₹10 lakh, margin ₹10 lakh → excess over ₹9 lakh = ₹1 lakh. Client Y: ₹20 lakh collateral, ₹15 lakh margin → nil. TM prop margin ₹80 lakh. Load = ₹81 lakh = 81%: not in RRM.

sections.title: Derivatives: Initial Margin and SPAN

blocks.text: Initial margin is payable upfront by clearing members on all open positions, down to client level. It includes SPAN margin, margin on consolidated crystallised obligation, delivery margin and any additional margin the CC specifies. Client positions are netted per client and grossed across clients (no set-off between clients); proprietary positions are netted at TM/CM level with no set-off against clients. Margins are aggregated first at TM level, then at CM level.

SPAN (Standard Portfolio Analysis of Risk, developed by the Chicago Mercantile Exchange) computes real-time initial margin as the worst scenario loss on a client's whole portfolio of futures and options on the same underlying, across maturities and across price and volatility scenarios. It is based on 99% VaR over a horizon set by the product's Margin Period of Risk.

VaR = maximum likely price change over a given interval (horizon) at a given confidence level (percentile). SPAN improves on it in two ways: 16 'what-if' scenarios, and margin on the entire portfolio, not position by position.
Long 1 lot Nifty futures + long 1 lot Nifty puts: in a crash the futures lose and the puts gain. SPAN values both together in each scenario, so the margin is far below the sum of the two legs.
blocks.title: Why portfolio margining matters

items: Margin Period of Risk (MPOR): set by the CC per product based on liquidity, minimum 2 days; initial margin is scaled up accordingly.

Risk parameters: contracts are valued under the 16 scenarios (scenario contract values), then applied to actual portfolios in real time. Values are updated at least 5 times a day: previous close, 11:00 a.m., 12:30 p.m., 2:00 p.m., end of day.

blocks.text: Cash segment VaR = 99.9%; derivatives SPAN = 99% VaR.

sections.title: Derivatives: Other Margins, ELM and Cross Margining

blocks.text: Calendar spread = long one expiry and short another of the same underlying. The legs largely offset, so a smaller spread charge applies, based on the delta of the portfolio in each month (near-month option delta 100 + far-month option delta −100 = same charge as long 100 near / short 100 far futures).
Long 1 lot Nifty current-month futures, short 1 lot next-month futures. Far month value ₹15,00,000 → spread charge 1.75% = ₹26,250, far below margin on two naked legs.
blocks.title: Calendar spread charge

blocks.text: Expiry day. Basis risk is high on expiry day (the expiring contract can move very differently from later ones) and volumes are huge, so the calendar spread benefit is not available on expiry day for contracts expiring that day.

SEBI circular of February 05, 2026: existing calendar spread margins stay unchanged for all expiries except contracts expiring that day. If monthly expiries fall on the 29th (current), 30th (next) and 31st (far), then on the 29th, spreads of 29th + 30th or 29th + 31st get no calendar spread treatment, while spreads of 30th + 31st continue to get it.

Margin on consolidated crystallised obligation: money a client already owes but has not settled. If the client-level net is payable, that amount is the margin; released on completion of settlement. MTM must be paid by all members before trading starts next day.

Net Option Value (NOV) = long option value − short option value (last close, updated intraday). It is added to the CM's liquid net worth, so option MTM gains/losses adjust net worth and are not settled in cash.
LNW ₹1 crore; clients long options worth ₹20 lakh and short options worth ₹35 lakh. NOV = −₹15 lakh, so effective LNW = ₹85 lakh.

blocks.text: Upfront premium from option buyers. Options are non-linear, highly leveraged and timed, so to prevent undue intraday leverage SEBI requires TMs/CMs to collect premium upfront; upfront margin includes net options premium payable, verified in intraday snapshots with penalties. Applies in equity derivatives from February 01, 2025.
Delivery margin (physically settled contracts): on the lower of potential deliverable positions or in-the-money long options, from 4 days before expiry. Thursday expiry → from previous Friday EOD.

blocks.text: Options ELM is charged only on short positions (buyers have already paid premium), at the same rates as futures: index 2%, stock 3.5%.
Expiry-day tail cover: an additional 2% ELM on short index options expiring that day, both those open at day start and those written during the day.
Short Nifty options expiring today, notional ₹50 lakh: normal ELM 2% (₹1 lakh) + expiry-day 2% (₹1 lakh) = ₹2 lakh.

Volatile stocks: the cash segment triggers apply in F&O too; minimum total margin (SPAN + ELM + additional) = maximum intraday move. Additional margins may include surveillance margin, margin for volatile stocks, for securities in the ban period, or for client concentration. For strikes far from the close, the net short value is collected in cash on T+1 and held till expiry or square-up.

Cross margining (SEBI, December 02, 2008, all participants) lets offsetting cash and F&O positions share margin. Eligible pairs: index futures with constituent stock futures or cash stocks; ETF with constituent stock futures or cash stocks; index futures with ETF; stock futures with the same cash stock; index futures on eligible indices; and highly correlated indices.

items: Constituent baskets must be a complete replica of the index in the specified ratio. Same CM or different CMs both qualify.
Futures legs must be in the same expiry month for the basic benefit. Computed client-wise in real time; for institutions, after trade confirmation.
Highly correlated indices: correlation > 0.90; ≥ 80% common constituents; smaller index's constituents ≥ 80% weight in the larger.
With different expiries, the benefit is revoked at the start of the expiry day of the first-expiring leg.

sections.title: Liquid Net Worth, Pre-trade Controls and Risk Disclosures

blocks.text: Liquid Net Worth (LNW) = liquid assets deposited for initial margin and capital adequacy minus initial margin and ELM on total gross open positions. It must never fall below ₹50 lakh.
Deposit ₹3 crore; initial margin ₹1.8 crore; ELM ₹0.5 crore. LNW = ₹70 lakh. If initial margin rises to ₹2.1 crore, LNW = ₹40 lakh: a breach.

Derivatives pre-trade controls: quantity freeze, price band, dynamic price band, trade execution range, self-trade check. RRM applies at 90% utilisation, as in cash. Brokers must show SEBI's F&O Risk disclosures on their websites and to clients, as a login pop-up the client must acknowledge before proceeding, covering at least 50% of the screen.

sections.title: Position Limits and Open Interest

blocks.text: Position limits stop anyone building positions big enough to manipulate prices or cause a large default. They apply by instrument, broker, clearing member, FPI/MF, non-institutional client and market-wide; violations attract penalties.

Under SEBI's May 29, 2025 circular, OI is measured at portfolio level as the net delta-adjusted position across futures and options (FutEq OI), added across all UCCs. Delta: long futures +1; long call 0 to +1; long put 0 to −1; short call negative; short put positive.
Long 2 lots futures + long 4 lots calls of delta 0.5 = 2 + 2 = 4 lots FutEq.

MWPL (single stock) = lower of 15% of free float and 65 × ADDV, with a floor of 10% of free float. Once market-wide OI exceeds 95% of MWPL, only position-reducing trades are allowed (ban period). A passive rise from delta movement is not a breach.
Free float ₹10,000 crore (15% = ₹1,500 crore); ADDV ₹20 crore (65× = ₹1,300 crore). MWPL = ₹1,300 crore; ban above ₹1,235 crore.

items: Index futures/options limits are at PAN level, checked against total market OI at previous day end; breaches caused only by a fall in market OI are passive, not violations.
Derivatives pre-open: current-month stock and index futures; in the last 5 trading days before expiry, also next-month futures.
Index derivative limits are now monitored intraday, with an entity-level framework for index options using at least 4 random snapshots a day.

blocks.text: 95% of MWPL = ban; 90% collateral = RRM; below 85% = normal mode.

sections.title: Margin Collection by the Clearing Corporation

items: Initial margin and ELM are payable upfront by CMs, who collect them upfront from clients. Any eligible liquid asset, in combinations within CC limits.
CMs may give own, TM-proprietary or client securities, but can re-pledge client/TM securities only via the Margin Pledge facility of NSDL and CDSL.

If an entity's margin exceeds its allocated collateral plus re-pledged securities, the TM's/CM's proprietary collateral is blocked as deemed allocation. Allocated + re-pledged collateral must always cover the minimum margin.
CCs allow intraday inter-segment collateral transfer, and release of collateral intraday and at EOD.

blocks.text: A client's margin at the CC is ₹12 lakh; allocated cash ₹8 lakh + re-pledged shares ₹2 lakh = ₹10 lakh. The ₹2 lakh gap is blocked from the TM's proprietary collateral (then the CM's).

sections.title: Protecting Client Collateral

blocks.text: 1. Margin pledge (SEBI, February 25, 2020): client securities collateral only by margin pledge in the depository, into a TM/CM demat tagged 'Client Securities Margin Pledge Account'. Chain: client → TM → CM (from TM's account) → CC (approved securities, UCC-wise), with the full trail in the client's demat.

items: Re-pledged securities give exposure to that client only; the CM gets none. Non-approved securities may be pledged to the TM/CM as per their own lists.
On a client trade, the CC first blocks the CM's collateral and releases it (latest by end of day) to the extent of the client's re-pledged securities.

sections.title: Running Account Settlement and Unpaid Securities

blocks.text: Without the client's written running account authorisation, funds are settled within 1 working day of pay-out. With it, settlement is quarterly or monthly as the client chooses: a gap of at most 90 or 30 days. Since June 20, 2019 there is no running account for securities, so the rules cover funds only. On settlement the broker sends a statement of accounts (ledger extract, securities register extract, reasons for retention, pledge details) and may settle across segments of the same exchange.

Unpaid securities. If a client buys but does not pay in full, the broker should neither keep the shares in its own pool nor release them free. The answer: shares go to the client, padlocked for the broker.

For trades not under MTF, unpaid securities are paid out to the client's demat and auto-pledged (no client instruction needed) with reason 'unpaid' to the TM's 'Client Unpaid Securities Pledgee Account' (CUSPA). The TM then emails/SMSes the client about the obligation and its right to sell. The TM must have a policy (standalone or in its Risk Management Policy), told to clients before it applies, with a maximum payment period of 5 trading days from pay-out.

flashcards.q: What does a CC's settlement guarantee mean?
flashcards.a: Funds and securities will be settled even if a broker or clearing member fails to meet its obligation.

flashcards.q: Name the three margins in the cash segment.
flashcards.a: VaR margin, Extreme Loss Margin and Mark to Market loss margin.

flashcards.q: What does VaR margin cover in the cash segment?
flashcards.a: The largest loss that can be expected on 99.9% of days.

flashcards.q: Which two measures decide a stock's liquidity group?
flashcards.a: Trading frequency over the previous six months (80% of days) and mean impact cost (1%).

flashcards.q: VaR margin for Group III (illiquid) securities?
flashcards.a: 50% if traded at least once a week on any exchange; 75% otherwise.

flashcards.q: What is scrip sigma?
flashcards.a: The security's volatility at the end of the previous trading day, computed by EWMA of daily returns.

flashcards.q: How is mean impact cost measured?
flashcards.a: Price movement caused by a hypothetical ₹1 lakh order versus the mean of best bid and offer, from 4 daily snapshots.

flashcards.q: ELM in the cash segment?
flashcards.a: 3.5% for any stock; 2% for ETFs on broad-based indices.

flashcards.q: Which older terms did 'Extreme Loss Margin' replace?
flashcards.a: 'Exposure limits' and 'second line of defence'.

flashcards.q: Upfront margin for securities in Trade for Trade Surveillance?
flashcards.a: 100% (VaR + ELM).

flashcards.q: Can one client's MTM profit offset another client's MTM loss?
flashcards.a: No. MTM is netted within a client but grossed across clients; only losses are added at broker level.

flashcards.q: What is ICMTM?
flashcards.a: Intraday Crystallised MTM: the loss on trades opened and closed the same day, at weighted average prices, blocked in real time.

flashcards.q: What four requirements must liquid assets cover?
flashcards.a: MTM losses, VaR margin, Extreme Loss Margin and Base Minimum Capital.

flashcards.q: Can non-cash liquid assets be used to pay MTM losses?
flashcards.a: No. MTM must be paid in cash or cash equivalents.

flashcards.q: BMC for a broker that uses algorithmic trading?
flashcards.a: ₹50 lakh, whatever its client/proprietary mix.

flashcards.q: BMC for a broker on several segments of the same exchange?
flashcards.a: The highest BMC among those segments, not the total.

flashcards.q: Effect of early pay-in of securities on margins?
flashcards.a: That position is excluded from margins; all margins are deemed collected and no short-collection penalty arises.

flashcards.q: What does a kill switch do?
flashcards.a: Cancels all of a member's outstanding orders with a single command.

flashcards.q: What triggers and ends risk reduction mode?
flashcards.a: Starts at 90% collateral utilisation; normal mode resumes when it falls below 85%.

flashcards.q: What is SPAN and who developed it?
flashcards.a: Standard Portfolio Analysis of Risk, from the Chicago Mercantile Exchange: portfolio margin from the worst of 16 scenarios.

flashcards.q: Minimum Margin Period of Risk for equity derivatives?
flashcards.a: 2 days, set per product based on its liquidity.

flashcards.q: Calendar spread charges?
flashcards.a: Index derivatives: 1.75% of far month contract. Single stock derivatives: 2.2% of far month contract.

flashcards.q: On expiry day, which calendar spreads lose the spread benefit?
flashcards.a: Only spreads with a leg in the contract expiring that day; spreads between later expiries keep it.

flashcards.q: What is Net Option Value and where does it go?
flashcards.a: Long option value minus short option value; added to the CM's liquid net worth. Option MTM is not settled in cash.

flashcards.q: From when must option buyers pay premium upfront?
flashcards.a: February 01, 2025, in the equity derivatives segment.

flashcards.q: When do delivery margins start on physically settled contracts?
flashcards.a: Four days before expiry; for a Thursday expiry, from the previous Friday EOD.

flashcards.q: Additional ELM on options expiry day?
flashcards.a: 2% on short index options expiring that day, both those open at day start and those written during the day.

flashcards.q: Define liquid net worth of a clearing member.
flashcards.a: Liquid assets minus initial margin and ELM on gross open positions; must stay at least ₹50 lakh.

flashcards.q: How is MWPL for a single stock computed?
flashcards.a: Lower of 15% of free float and 65 × ADDV, with a floor of 10% of free float.

flashcards.q: What is FutEq OI?
flashcards.a: Net delta-adjusted open position across futures and options of an underlying, added up across all UCCs.

flashcards.q: Derivatives: deadline to collect delivery margin and consolidated crystallised obligation margin?
flashcards.a: By T+1.

flashcards.q: How is the peak margin penalty computed?
flashcards.a: On the higher of the EOD shortfall and the peak (snapshot) shortfall; minimum 4 snapshots a day.

flashcards.q: What is the 'Client Securities Margin Pledge Account'?
flashcards.a: The separate demat account a TM/CM opens to receive clients' margin pledges and to re-pledge them onward.

flashcards.q: What is DDPI?
flashcards.a: Demat Debit and Pledge Instruction: used for settlement transfers and pledges/re-pledges in place of a Power of Attorney.

flashcards.q: USCNBA vs DSCNBA?
flashcards.a: Up Streaming account receives client funds; Down Streaming account is the only account for paying clients.

flashcards.q: Which client funds forms can be upstreamed to the CC?
flashcards.a: Cash, lien on FDRs from client funds, or pledge of overnight MF scheme units bought with client funds.

flashcards.q: What is CUSPA?
flashcards.a: Client Unpaid Securities Pledgee Account: the TM account to which unpaid (non-MTF) securities are auto-pledged in the client's demat.

flashcards.q: Key CUSPA timelines?
flashcards.a: Client pays within 5 trading days of pay-out; auto-release at end of 6th; extension request by 6 p.m. on 5th day.

flashcards.q: Can a TM give exposure against, or bank-pledge, CUSPA securities?
flashcards.a: Neither. They may count for margin reporting, but give no exposure and cannot go to banks/NBFCs.

flashcards.q: When must the Annual Global Statement be issued?
flashcards.a: Within 30 days from the end of the financial year.

flashcards.q: CTR, STR and NTR deadlines?
flashcards.a: CTR and NTR by the 15th of the next month; STR within 7 days of concluding suspicion.

flashcards.q: Four steps of Risk Based Supervision?
flashcards.a: Risk assessment, risk and impact rating, supervisory risk rating score, supervisory approach.

flashcards.q: Parameters for QSB designation?
flashcards.a: Active clients, client assets, trading volumes, clients' EOD margin obligations and proprietary trading volumes.

flashcards.q: Core SGF contribution shares?
flashcards.a: CC at least 50% of MRC, stock exchange at least 25%, all clearing members together at most 25%.

flashcards.q: Who manages the Core SGF?
flashcards.a: The Regulatory Oversight Committee (ROC) of the clearing corporation.

flashcards.q: First and last layers of the default waterfall?
flashcards.a: First: the defaulting member's own monies. Last: pro-rata haircut to pay-outs.

questions.q: Which of the following is a risk containment measure used by a clearing corporation?
options: Checking margin requirements
Checking the net worth of the client/investor
Checking whether the order placed is genuine
Checking the client's income tax returns
questions.why: CC risk containment includes stringent margin requirements, capital adequacy of members, position limits and online monitoring. Client net worth and order genuineness are not CC risk measures.

questions.q: The SPAN method of computing margin is used for trades in which segment?
options: Equity cash segment
Government securities segment
Futures and Options segment
Mutual fund distribution platform
questions.why: CCs use SPAN (a CME product) for real-time initial margin on futures and options portfolios.

questions.q: Which of the following statements on record keeping by stock brokers is true?
options: The sauda book (register of transactions) needs to be kept for only 2 years
Under the SEBI (Stock Broker) Regulations, 2026, books of account and records must be preserved for at least eight years
Members' contract books must be kept for 10 years under Rule 15 of SCRR
Records may be destroyed once the exchange has completed its annual inspection
questions.why: Regulation 16 of the SEBI (Stock Broker) Regulations, 2026 requires books and records maintained under Regulation 15 to be preserved for a minimum of eight years.

questions.q: How often must brokers send a Global Statement to their clients?
options: Monthly
Quarterly
Half-yearly
Annually
questions.why: SEBI's letter of November 27, 2017 requires an Annual Global Statement, issued within 30 days from the end of the financial year.

questions.q: Cash and cash equivalents must make up at least what share of a member's liquid assets?
questions.why: Cash equivalents must be at least 50% of liquid assets; other liquid assets above the cash-equivalent amount are not counted.

questions.q: A market-wide index movement of what size halts trading for the rest of the day, whatever the time of breach?
questions.why: A 20% movement in Sensex or Nifty 50 halts trading for the remainder of the day at any time. A 10% or 15% breach halts trading for a limited period if it happens early in the day.

questions.q: In the equity cash segment, which margin is collected upfront along with ELM?
options: Mark to market margin
SPAN margin
Delivery margin
VaR margin
questions.why: In the cash segment, TMs/CMs must collect VaR margin and ELM upfront. MTM is collected later, and SPAN is the derivatives method.

questions.q: A stock enters the ban period, in which members and clients may only reduce positions, once market-wide open interest exceeds what share of its MWPL?
questions.why: Once market-wide OI in a scrip exceeds 95% of MWPL, positions can only be decreased through offsetting trades.

questions.q: Monthly expiries fall on the 29th (current), 30th (next) and 31st (far). On the 29th, which calendar spread position still gets calendar spread margin treatment?
options: A spread between the 29th and 30th contracts
A spread between the 29th and 31st contracts
None. All calendar spread benefit is withdrawn on any expiry day
A spread between the 30th and 31st contracts
questions.why: SEBI's February 05, 2026 clarification withdraws the benefit only for spreads involving the contract expiring that day. A 30th/31st spread keeps its treatment on the 29th.

questions.q: Why did SEBI decide that calendar spread benefit will not be available on expiry day for contracts expiring that day?
options: To increase transaction charges collected by exchanges
Because of significant basis risk and very large expiry-day volumes
Because calendar spreads are not permitted in index derivatives
Because SPAN cannot value far-month contracts on expiry day
questions.why: On expiry day the expiring contract can move very differently from later expiries (basis risk), and volumes are very large compared to other days.

questions.q: True or False: According to SEBI's circular of February 05, 2026, margin calculations for all calendar spread positions change on an expiry day, whichever contracts they involve.
options: True
False
questions.why: False. Existing calendar spread margin calculations stay unchanged for all expiries except contracts expiring on that given day.

questions.q: For a trade not covered by the margin trading facility, what happens to securities the client has not fully paid for at the time of pay-out?
options: They are transferred to the client's demat account and auto-pledged to the TM's CUSPA with reason 'unpaid'
They are kept in the TM's pool account until the client pays
They are pledged by the TM with a bank to fund the client's shortfall
They are returned to the clearing corporation for auction
questions.why: Unpaid securities are paid out directly to the client's demat account, followed by an auto-pledge (no client instruction needed) in favour of the Client Unpaid Securities Pledgee Account.

questions.q: If a pledge on unpaid securities is neither invoked nor released within five trading days after pay-out, what happens?
options: The TM may keep the pledge indefinitely until the client pays
The depository automatically invokes the pledge and sells the shares
The depositories automatically release the pledge at the end of the sixth trading day after pay-out
The securities move to the TM's proprietary demat account
questions.why: The depositories auto-release the pledge at the end of the sixth trading day after pay-out, and the securities become free balance for the client.

questions.q: A stock pledged to the CUSPA is stuck in a lower circuit with only sellers, so the TM cannot sell it within 5 trading days. What may the TM do?
options: Transfer it to its own demat account and sell it later
Request, by 6 p.m. on the fifth trading day after pay-out, an extension of the pledge for one additional calendar week
Request, by 6 p.m. on the sixth trading day, an extension for one more month
Re-pledge the stock to an NBFC until the circuit opens
questions.why: In exceptional cases like a lower circuit, suspension or other valid reasons, the TM may seek a one-calendar-week extension by 6 p.m. on the fifth trading day after pay-out, and must inform the client.

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT permitted for securities pledged to a TM's CUSPA?
options: Considering them for reporting client margin collection to the CC
Selling them in the market under the client's UCC after invocation
Releasing the pledge on excess securities on or before the next trading day
Pledging them to banks/NBFCs to raise funds
questions.why: CUSPA securities cannot be pledged or transferred to banks/NBFCs. They may count for margin reporting and can be sold under the client's UCC after invocation.

questions.q: True or False: Unpaid securities pledged to a TM's CUSPA may be counted for reporting client margin collection, and the TM may also give the client trading exposure against them.
options: True
False
questions.why: False. They may be counted for margin reporting to the CC, but the TM shall not provide any exposure to the client against them.

questions.q: What is the minimum VaR margin rate for a Group II (less liquid) security?
questions.why: Group II VaR is based on 6σ subject to a minimum of 21.5%. 9% is the Group I floor and 6% is the floor for broad-based index ETFs.

questions.q: At day end, a broker's clients show MTM results of: Client A −₹900, Client B −₹1,100, Client C +₹1,400. How much MTM must the broker deposit with the CC?
options: Nil
questions.why: MTM is grossed across clients and only losses are added: ₹900 + ₹1,100 = ₹2,000. Client C's profit is not set off.

questions.q: In the same settlement, Client P has a net buy position of ₹2,100 in Security X and Client Q a net sell position of ₹100 in Security X. What gross open position does the CC use for the member's VaR margin in X?
questions.why: Positions are netted within each client and grossed across clients: ₹2,100 + ₹100 = ₹2,200.

questions.q: In a cash market purchase, which combination of margins together cannot exceed the purchase value?
options: VaR margin and ELM only, with MTM levied over and above
VaR margin, ELM and MTM losses together
ELM and MTM only
There is no cap on margins for a purchase
questions.why: For a buy, VaR + ELM + MTM together cannot exceed the purchase value. For a sale, the cap covers only VaR + ELM, and MTM is levied in addition.

questions.q: If a custodian rejects an institutional trade, on whom are the margins levied?
options: The custodian
The institutional investor directly
The member who executed the trade
The Core Settlement Guarantee Fund
questions.why: Margins on custodian-confirmed institutional trades are levied on the custodian. On rejected or unaccepted trades they are levied on the executing member.

questions.q: What is the BMC deposit for a stock broker doing both proprietary and client trading, without algorithmic trading?
options: ₹10 lakh
₹15 lakh
₹50 lakh
₹25 lakh
questions.why: BMC: ₹10 lakh (prop only), ₹15 lakh (clients only), ₹25 lakh (both, no algo), ₹50 lakh (any broker with algo).

questions.q: A stock broker in risk reduction mode returns to normal risk management mode when its collateral utilisation falls below:
questions.why: RRM starts at 90% utilisation, and the broker moves back to normal mode when utilisation is below the CC's level, currently 85%.

questions.q: Which of these orders will NOT be accepted from a stock broker in risk reduction mode?
options: Non-margined orders
Orders that reduce the open position
Immediate or Cancel orders
Fresh orders backed by sufficient margin
questions.why: In RRM only IOC orders are allowed, risk-reducing orders are accepted and new orders are checked for margin, but non-margined orders are not accepted at all.

questions.q: What is the minimum liquid net worth a clearing member must maintain at all times?
options: ₹25 lakh
₹50 lakh
₹1 crore
₹10 lakh
questions.why: Liquid net worth (liquid assets minus initial margin and ELM) must never fall below ₹50 lakh.

questions.q: If a physically settled derivative contract expires on a Thursday, from when do delivery margins on potential in-the-money long options apply?
options: From the previous Friday EOD (four days before expiry)
From the Wednesday before expiry
Only on expiry day
From T+1 after expiry
questions.why: Delivery margins start four days before expiry; the workbook's example is a Thursday expiry, with margins from the previous Friday EOD.

questions.q: On options expiry day, what additional ELM is levied on short index options expiring that day?
questions.why: To raise tail-risk cover on expiry day, an additional 2% ELM applies on short index options expiring that day, both those open at day start and those written during the day.

questions.q: Under cross margining, what spread margin applies to offsetting positions in correlated indices with different expiry dates?
questions.why: Correlated indices: 30% with the same expiry, 40% with different expiries. 35% applies to an index against its constituents with a different expiry, and 25% to the basic eligible offsets.

questions.q: Under the peak margin framework, which shortfall is used to levy the penalty on a TM/CM?
options: The sum of the EOD shortfall and the peak shortfall
Only the EOD shortfall
The higher of the EOD shortfall and the peak shortfall
The average shortfall across all snapshots
questions.why: EOD obligation is compared with EOD margin available and peak obligation with peak margin available; the higher of the two shortfalls is penalised.

questions.q: When a trade comes from a client account, in what order does the CC block margin?
options: Client collateral, then TM proprietary collateral, then CM proprietary collateral
CM proprietary collateral, then TM proprietary collateral, then client collateral
TM proprietary collateral, then client collateral, then CM proprietary collateral
Client collateral, then CM proprietary collateral, then TM proprietary collateral
questions.why: Margin is first blocked from the client's collateral, then from the TM's proprietary collateral, and finally from the CM's proprietary collateral.

questions.q: Within what time must a Suspicious Transaction Report (STR) be filed with FIU-IND?
options: By the 15th of the succeeding month
Within 7 days of arriving at a conclusion that the transaction is suspicious
Within 30 days of the transaction
Within 24 hours of the transaction
questions.why: STR is due within 7 days of concluding that a transaction is suspicious. CTR and NTR are monthly, due by the 15th of the next month.

questions.q: If a client has authorised a running account, what is the maximum gap between two settlements of the client's funds?
options: 90 days (quarterly) or 30 days (monthly), as the client chooses
60 days or 15 days
180 days or 90 days
One year
questions.why: The client chooses quarterly or monthly settlement, so the gap can be at most 90 or 30 days.

questions.q: What is the clearing corporation's minimum contribution to the Core SGF?
options: 25% of MRC
Not more than 25% of MRC
At least 50% of MRC, from its own funds
100% of MRC
questions.why: The CC contributes at least 50% of the MRC from its own funds, the stock exchange at least 25%, and all clearing members together not more than 25%.

questions.q: In the default waterfall, which resource is used first?
options: Insurance, if any
Penalties in the Core SGF
CC resources equal to 5% of the segment MRC
Monies of the defaulting member, including its Core SGF contribution and excess monies in other segments
questions.why: The defaulter's own monies come first, then insurance, then CC resources of 5% of segment MRC, then the Core SGF (penalties first).

questions.q: In the derivatives segment, what is the maximum capped additional contribution by a non-defaulting member to cover a default?
options: Lower of 2 times its primary contribution or 20% of the segment's Core SGF
Lower of 2 times its primary contribution or 10% of the segment's Core SGF
3 times its primary contribution
There is no cap
questions.why: Derivatives segment: lower of 2× primary contribution or 20% of Core SGF on the date of default. Equity/debt segments use 10% instead of 20%.
